records.text: Jeffrey Epstein and Jean-Luc Brunel trafficked through modeling organizations such as MC2 Model Management; Owens also linked their activity to Victoria's Secret and Miss Universe.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: the way that he was moving with Jean-Luc Brunel and going to these industries like Victoria's Secret like Miss Universe and I think that's how Trump is caught up into it and is also being rinsed out of these files they were trafficking through these organizations we know this for a fact modeling organizations like MC2 Model Management

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Victim testimony and reporting support that Epstein used modeling access and a false Victoria's Secret recruiter pretext, and that associates connected to MC2 supplied or introduced models. The broader statement that he trafficked girls through MC2, Victoria's Secret, and Miss Universe as three established channels overstates the record: Epstein held no formal Victoria's Secret role, and reliable evidence for a Miss Universe trafficking channel was not found.

Now, Jean-Luc Brunel, he was taken into custody on counts of rape and sexual assault on a minor under the age of 15, rape and sexual assault on a minor over 15, sexual harassment, criminal associations, human trafficking to the detriment of minor victims for the purposes of sexual exploitation.

verification.notes: Contemporaneous reporting based on the Paris prosecutors office confirms that Jean-Luc Brunel was detained at Charles de Gaulle Airport on December 16, 2020 as part of an investigation covering rape, sexual assault of minors, sexual harassment, criminal association, and trafficking or exploitation of minors. Later formal charges were narrower, so this result verifies the scope of the investigation at custody rather than implying conviction or formal charge on every listed offense.

records.text: Owens said Epstein gave Brunel seed money in 2005 to start MC2 Model Management in Paris.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And why were he and Jeffrey Epstein so close? Well, because in 2005, Jeffrey Epstein gave him the seed money for him to start the modeling agency MC2 in Paris.

verification.notes: Reliable reporting and a sworn former-bookkeeper account confirm that Epstein backed MC2 in 2005 with a 1 million dollar line of credit. However, MC2 was formed from the U.S. arm of Karin Models and operated from Miami and New York, not Paris. The funding component is true but the stated location is wrong.

records.text: Owens said Jean-Luc and Arnaud Brunel founded Next Model Corporation in New York City, from which Next Model Management developed.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: He was actually the founder. ... alongside his brother Arnaud Brunel, of a modeling agency in New York City, one called Next Model Management. ... Jean-Luc Brunel and his brother founded the Next Model Corporation. And from that spun the next model management modeling agency.

verification.notes: New York corporate records reported by reliable outlets identify Jean-Luc and Arnaud Brunel as founders of Next Management Corporation in 1988. In 1989 the Brunels participated with Faith Kates in forming Next Model Management, in which the brothers held a minority interest. This supports the stated corporate sequence, while later company histories emphasize Kates and Joel Wilkenfeld as the enduring founders.

records.text: Owens cited a current class-action lawsuit naming Next Model Management and MC2 as defendants in allegations that underage models' pay was deducted by as much as 70%, keeping them dependent while the industry controlled their work, money, access, and housing.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: In fact, there is a current class action lawsuit that's making its way through the court system right now against next model management. ... They're named as a defendant alongside MC2, Jean-Luc Brunel's agency named as defendants. ... Paychecks deducted up to 70%, which kept them dependent as underaged workers while the industry completely controlled their work, completely controlled their money, their access, their housing. ... Like I said, Jean-Luc Brunel, who is now dead, and MC2, which he ran, and Faith Kates and Next Model Management, which he started with Faith Kates, are all listed as defendants in these allegations, which span back decades.

verification.notes: Shanklin v. Wilhelmina is a real, continuing certified class action involving Next and alleged unlawful deductions, wage-statement failures, and misclassification. The current official notice names Wilhelmina and Next as defendants, not MC2, and does not frame the certified claims specifically around underage models or a universal deduction as high as 70 percent. The core lawsuit claim is true but important details are overstated or outdated.

records.text: Owens cited released passenger manifests as indicating that John C. Phelan flew twice on Jeffrey Epstein's plane in 2006, including a London-to-New York flight with Epstein and Jean-Luc Brunel.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: passenger manifests that were released as part of the Epstein files indicate that Phelan flew twice on the plane of Jeffrey Epstein several months before Epstein's first arrest on sex charges. ... The manifest for the second flight from London to New York on March 3, 2006 indicates that Phelan flew with 12 other passengers, including Epstein, modeling agent and Epstein associate Jean-Luc Brunel.

verification.notes: Released passenger manifests and independent current reporting identify John Phelan on two transatlantic Epstein-plane flights in 2006. One manifest covers a London-to-New York flight and lists Epstein and a misspelled rendering of Jean-Luc Brunel. This verifies the limited manifest claim; presence on a flight does not by itself imply criminal conduct.
